_source: CLAUDE.md §39 PERFORMANCE METRICS. The twenty-three entries below are §39's own list, in §39's own order and wording. scripts/tests/test_performance.py parses them back out of CLAUDE.md, so a twenty-fourth bullet in the spec fails the build rather than going unimplemented.
_reader: scripts/performance.py is the ONE computer. A caller that wants a §39 number asks it; nothing else may define one, because a second definition of 'expectancy' is how two reports of the same trades disagree.
_sample_size: §39: 'Always show sample size.' Every result carries `n`, and `n` is not a metric that can be dropped by a caller selecting fields -- performance.metrics() puts it at the top level and refuses to omit it. A metric whose sample is below its own `min_n` is returned as unavailable(), not as a number with a caveat somewhere else on the page.
_no_universal_score: §39: 'Do not optimize against a single universal metric.' There is no weighted composite here and performance.py has no `score()`. What it has is `refuse_universal_score()`, whose body raises. Ranking is the caller's business and must be lexicographic over several named metrics (scripts/rank-setups.py), never a single blended number.

kinds.ratio: a fraction in 0..1, rendered as a percentage by the caller
kinds.r_multiple: a multiple of the risked amount (R); unit-free and account-size-free
kinds.currency: account currency; depends on the account profile's size and per-trade risk
kinds.probability: an estimated probability in 0..1 -- ALWAYS with its method and its assumptions attached
kinds.duration: a span, carried in bars AND as a wall-clock span when the series says what a bar is

metrics.definition: Every CLOSED trade in the population, whatever its outcome. Not the number of signals, and not the number of decisions: a blocked entry is §41's evaluation state, not a trade.
Trades with R strictly greater than the breakeven band. §39 lists breakeven SEPARATELY from wins and losses, so a flat trade belongs to neither.
Trades with R strictly below the breakeven band.

Trades whose R lies inside the breakeven band (|R| <= breakeven_band, default 0.05R, and any record whose engine labelled it 'breakeven'). A THIRD bucket, because §39 asks for one: before 2026-09-18 `journal.stats()` folded R<=0 into losses, which put every flat trade in the win-rate denominator and extended the losing streak through it.

wins / total_trades. Breakeven trades stay in the DENOMINATOR -- they happened -- but never in the numerator. Reported beside `breakeven` so the reader can compute the other convention if they want it.

Mean R per trade, over every trade including breakeven. Identical in value to average_R for an R-denominated population; both are listed because §39 lists both, and they diverge the moment a caller passes position-weighted R.
Mean of the per-trade R multiples, unweighted. Reported with `average_win_R` and `average_loss_R`, which is what makes an expectancy readable.
gross win R / |gross loss R|. Undefined with no losing trade -- returned as unavailable(), never as infinity and never as a large placeholder number, because a placeholder sorts.
Realised profit and loss in account currency. Requires an account: R is account-free, money is not. Without a starting balance and a per-trade risk fraction this is unavailable rather than assumed.
Largest peak-to-trough fall of the equity curve, as a fraction of the peak. Also reported in R (`max_drawdown_R`) so an account-free population still has the number.

Mean depth of the COMPLETED drawdown episodes (peak -> trough -> recovery to that peak). An episode still open at the end of the series is included with a flag, because dropping it would flatter a curve that ends underwater -- which is the case that matters.
Longest run of consecutive winning trades. A breakeven trade BREAKS a run rather than extending it: it is not a win.
Longest run of consecutive losing trades. A breakeven trade breaks this run too -- the pre-2026-09-18 code extended it, which overstated the worst streak wherever management moved a stop to entry.

Maximum Favourable Excursion: the best unrealised R a trade reached between entry and exit. Reported as the mean over the population plus the mean for winners and losers separately -- 'losers that went to +2R first' is the whole reason the metric exists. §37 explicitly allows future bars to determine it (it is an outcome, not a decision).
metrics.implemented_by: scripts/performance.py metrics() -> mfe; produced by scripts/backtest-methods.py walk()

metrics.definition: Maximum Adverse Excursion: the worst unrealised R a trade reached before its exit, as a NEGATIVE number. Mean over the population plus winners/losers separately -- 'winners that first went to -0.9R' is what tells you whether the stop has any room.
metrics.implemented_by: scripts/performance.py metrics() -> mae; produced by scripts/backtest-methods.py walk()

metrics.definition: mean(R) / stdev(R) over the per-trade series, times sqrt(trades per year) when the population can date itself. PER-TRADE and un-annualised when it cannot -- and it SAYS which, because an un-annualised Sharpe next to an annualised one is a factor of ten. Risk-free rate is taken as zero and that assumption travels in the result.

As Sharpe but with the downside deviation (RMS of the negative part below the target return, target = 0) in the denominator. Unavailable when nothing was negative: a Sortino with no downside is not infinite, it is unmeasured.
net profit / max drawdown, both in the same unit (R by default). How many times over the strategy earned back its own worst hole.

Probability of reaching the account's ruin threshold within the declared horizon, by BOOTSTRAP over the observed per-trade R distribution (resampled with replacement, fixed seed, count declared). Not the closed-form gambler's-ruin formula: that assumes fixed win/loss sizes, which a 3R-target system does not have. The estimate carries its method, iterations, seed, horizon and threshold -- a probability without those is a decoration.

Probability of breaching ANY of the account profile's failure conditions (§33: max daily loss, max total drawdown, trailing drawdown) within the horizon -- a strictly wider event than ruin, and for a funded or prop account usually a much more likely one. Same bootstrap, same declared assumptions. Requires a real account profile from docs/architecture/account-profiles.json; there is no default account.

Probability of reaching the profit target before breaching any failure condition and within the minimum trading days -- i.e. passing the challenge. Defined here, and computed by the same bootstrap, but it is UNAVAILABLE for every account profile that declares no profit target: a personal account cannot be passed. That is a property of the profile, not a gap in the metric.

For trades that reached their target, the span from entry to that exit -- median and mean, in bars and in wall-clock when the timeframe is known. Losers and timeouts are excluded from the average and COUNTED separately, because a mean over only the winners is a survivorship claim unless the denominator is shown next to it.

Share of the series spent below a previous equity peak, plus the longest single underwater stretch. The fraction and the longest stretch are both reported: a strategy underwater 60 % of the time in short dips is a different thing from one that spent a single unbroken year there.

_sample_size_floors: `min_n` is the point below which a metric cannot be COMPUTED at all (a bootstrap over 4 outcomes has almost nothing to resample). It is NOT a confidence judgement. The three probability metrics carry a second, softer field: `low_confidence_below` -- above min_n and below it the metric IS computed and returned, with `low_confidence: true`, its `sample`, and a spread across bootstrap batches so the reader sees how wide the estimate is. User decision 2026-09-19: a wide number that says it is wide beats a refusal, because a prop-account question ('would this setup have passed?') has an answer at n=14 and hiding it helped nobody. §39 'always show sample size' is satisfied by SHOWING it, not by withholding.
